title: search --rows: typo'd object name silently ignored (unknown bound -> UNKNOWN, no hint)
description: crates/catherine-cli args parsing (parse_rows): --rows Objet=4 for an undeclared object is dropped without a word; search maps only schema.objects keys, so the typo yields zero rows -> UNKNOWN with empty scope and no explanation. Fix: emit envelope warning (warnings channel exists) naming the ignored object, or bad_argument. Warning preferred (keeps exit semantics).

title: parse: any minor version accepted (1.99 parses clean) — forward-compat gamble
description: crates/catherine-core/src/parse.rs accepts every minor of major 1: REPRODUCED format_version 1.99 -> exit 0. Docs say 'additive minors of the current major' but a future 1.x with semantics this build doesn't know gets silently misinterpreted. Fix: track KNOWN_MINOR (currently 0), reject minor > KNOWN_MINOR with unsupported_version; golden fixture + fixture-table update. Confirm against openspec add-model-document-kernel scenario wording first (may be deliberate policy — adjudicate before coding).
acceptance_criteria: 1.1+ rejected with unsupported_version until KNOWN_MINOR raised; fixtures pin both sides

title: distinguish: second document's schema silently discarded — cross-schema equivocation
description: crates/catherine-cli/src/runners.rs:181 builds typed_b as TypedInstance::build(&model.schema /* FIRST doc */, &second.instance). The second document's own schema is parsed then dropped. REPRODUCED: two fixtures whose arrow f points OPPOSITE directions (A: a->b, B: b->a) report {ok:true, outcome: equivalent-in-scope} — B's f-table (keyed over b rows) is reinterpreted as A's a->b table. Violates the product's honesty contract. Fix (TDD): red CLI test with opposite-direction fixtures (repro at /tmp/ct-repro/dist_b.ct.json); precondition second.schema == model.schema, else labeled error code schema_mismatch, exit 1, stderr envelope. This is input validation, not a schema-equivalence claim (spec boundary intact).
acceptance_criteria: differing schemas exit 1 with schema_mismatch; identical schemas unchanged behavior; CLI test added

title: search: is_clean counts proposed-equation violations — contract drift, latent unsound Contradiction
description: crates/catherine-analysis/src/search.rs:226 is_clean() = checks::check(schema,&typed).is_empty(), but check() emits violations for PROPOSED equations too (label hypothesized). Module docs (lines 27-28) and is_clean's own docstring promise 'only accepted equations constrain the search'. MASKED IN V1 (verified empirically): the lex-smallest fully-resolved candidate is the all-row-0 constant map, which collapse-satisfies every path equation, so verdicts cannot change today. GOES LIVE the moment inequality/injectivity/row-lower-bound constraints enter the language (DESIGN roadmap): witness rejection and UNSOUND executed-labeled Contradiction claims over the accepted scope. Zero test coverage: 'proposed' appears nowhere in crates/catherine-analysis/tests/. Fix (TDD): red test — schema with accepted set satisfiable + proposed equation rejecting non-constant candidates; assert Witness returned and is_clean unit-accepts an accepted-clean/proposed-dirty instance. Predicate: no Dangling findings AND no Violation with label Executed.
acceptance_criteria: proposed-only violations never block a witness; contradiction scope claims stay sound; regression test added

title: PREVENTION-A: 'no silent paths' negative-input matrix across all CLI surfaces
description: Class A (fail-open boundaries) recurrence gate. Bugs catherine-18t/51v/0kw share one shape: malformed or context-mismatched input at a layer seam is silently dropped/reinterpreted instead of surfacing as a labeled error or envelope warning. Build ONE table-driven integration test (crates/catherine-cli/tests/negative_matrix.rs): rows = every CLI surface (check/findings/search/redundant/underconstraint/distinguish/query) x every malformed-input class (undeclared object/arrow names in flags, second-doc schema mismatch, out-of-range format_version, unknown seed, uncomposable observation, bad flag syntax); each row asserts labeled error (exit 1, stderr envelope, stable code) OR envelope warning — never silence. Also audit parser RawDoc/RawSchema/RawInstance structs for serde deny_unknown_fields. Review rule: a new flag or surface without a negative-matrix row is incomplete (add to ro5u checklist).
acceptance_criteria: negative matrix test exists, covers all 7 surfaces; deny_unknown_fields audit done; ro5u checklist updated

title: PREVENTION-B: spectacular scenarios for module-level behavioral claims (docs-as-contracts)
description: Class B (prose-code drift) recurrence gate. Bugs catherine-u3k/mrq: module docstrings make behavioral claims nothing tests ('only accepted equations constrain the search', 'leftmost-innermost'). In this codebase docstrings ARE the contract — make them executable via the existing ah/espectacular setup: (1) add declared scenarios to the add-bounded-analysis contract TOMLs for each behavioral claim in analysis module headers (start with search's accepted/proposed split — the missing scenario that let u3k ship); (2) adopt the practice that any module-header sentence of the form 'X never/only/always Y' gets a declared scenario or is downgraded to a documented-limit note; (3) wire 'ah check --run-tests' into pre-push lefthook block (ah check already runs pre-commit statically).
acceptance_criteria: search accepted/proposed scenario declared + tested; ah check --run-tests in pre-push; claim-scenario practice written into .wai reflections or AGENTS guidance

title: gates: hook exit-code fix is not durable — bd init regenerates swallowing wrappers
description: Fixed today by hand: .beads/hooks/{pre-commit,pre-push,prepare-commit-msg} now propagate lefthook exit codes (call_lefthook || exit). But these files are bd-generated (BEGIN/END BEADS INTEGRATION markers); the next bd init re-appends the beads block after call_lefthook WITHOUT exit capture, silently disarming pretender/ah/spk gates again. Options: (a) upstream fix in beads hook template, (b) ddl doctor check that flags the swallow pattern (grep call_lefthook line followed by unchecked continuation), (c) lefthook.yml-side workaround. Also realigned versions.ddl.toml pins (pretender 0.10.0, wai 2026.10.19, openspec 1.15.0, ah 0.12.0 added) — keep ddl doctor verifying them.
notes: Chosen approach (from failure-taxonomy review): option (c) self-defending gate — add a lefthook pre-commit command OUTSIDE the ddl-managed block that greps .beads/hooks/{pre-commit,pre-push,prepare-commit-msg} for the '_lh_exit' capture pattern after call_lefthook and fails with a remediation hint if the swallow pattern returns. Keeps the fix durable across bd init regenerations without waiting on upstream. Still worth filing the upstream beads issue as option (a).

title: PREVENTION-C: enum-variant coverage ratchet + diff-coverage pre-push gate

title: canonical: add symmetric-structure property ratchet for the WL-pruning assumption
description: crates/catherine-core/src/canonical.rs solve() prunes branches by partition_profile equality — a 1-WL automorphism assumption (CFI graphs are the known counterexample class; hash is P6 ledger identity). roundtrip.rs already proves rename-invariance on random models, but random models rarely generate heavily self-symmetric structures where pruning bites. Fix: proptest strategy biased toward symmetric instances (permuted rows of automorphism-rich graphs: complete bipartite, cycles, duplicated components); assert model_hash invariance under row permutation. Ratchet the documented assumption with executable evidence.

title: P9 adjunct: bogart corpus emits .ct.json instances (grounded-instance harness) — bogart-side, not kernel
description:
Extraction adapters for grounded instances live HERE (bogart/tooling side), NOT in catherine-core (C4/E2: kernel smallness dies in adapters; specodelic 3.3k-line crate is the cautionary tale). Catherine-side delta: at most a `source` provenance field on instances.
  Goal: agent proposes only the schema; instances come from deterministic extraction over the bogart corpus — findings become reality-checks on the agent's model: contradiction-with-data (schema says impossible, row exists), dangling-against-data, underconstraint-against-data.
  License: E4 + C6 (discovery pressure against real data; kata-8 effect on live corpora).
  RED: no corpus-to-instance path; instances are hand-authored only.
  GREEN: bogart emits .ct.json instances for a corpus slice; catherine check runs unchanged; contradiction-with-data finding carries the offending row as witness.
  REFACTOR: extraction contract documented in bogart README (reader recipe pattern).
  Validation (pre-registered, seeded-defect protocol): inject N known schema/data mismatches into the corpus slice; measure detection rate WITH witnesses; report misses honestly.
  anti_goals: no parsers in catherine-core; no adapter maintenance in kernel; no live/repo-filesystem coupling in catherine

title: P10: schema-diff — accreted/weakened/equivalent classification via schema-level distinguish + path-equation set diff (LICENSED: E4)
description:
Phase 10 (expansion, Rule-of-5 reviewed 2026-11-11). Verify agent schema EDITS, not just models: given two model-document schemas v1->v2, classify the edit:
  - accreted: constraints added only (wild thin-category accretion laws, E10)
  - weakened: path equation no longer enforced -> finding WITH WITNESS (instance valid in v2, invalid in v1) — the agent-drift detector
  - refactor-equivalent: same instance space, proven via distinguish (no separating witness)
  Built on EXISTING ops: schema-level distinguish + path-equation set diff. No new epistemic machinery: all findings map to existing kinds.
  License: E4 (migration axis = the unique validated capability axis). Kernel delta ceiling ~400 LOC (C4: smallness is a falsifiable claim).
  RED: no schema-diff op; silent constraint-weakening between schema versions undetected.
  GREEN: weakened/accreted/equivalent findings with witnesses; silent-weakening fixture -> weakened finding; refactor fixture -> equivalent proven; cosmetic-edit negative control -> ZERO findings.
  REFACTOR: diff result joins model document; op added to deterministic ops list.
  Validation (pre-registered): one silent-weakening kata (must catch) + one refactor kata (must pass) + cosmetic negative control (must be silent).
  GATED on P6 (catherine-9vv) stop-condition verdict and P7 (catherine-alr) landing. Not filed before P6 per expansion-licensing rule (bd memory).
  anti_goals: no claims ledger; no persistence; no property-synthesis writer; no Sigma/Pi; no adapters in kernel
  openspec_change: add-schema-diff

Port bogart's prose spec invariants into .ct.json models checked in bogart's CI: (1) corpus-storage FTS-anchor equation block->document->edition = block->edition + block->document totality (violation+dangling classes); (2) stable_ids identity-domain disjointness aviso-vs-section (rule-lens preview, P8); (3) backfill selector capture_ambiguous/capture_unavailable as overlap/gap findings; (4) raw-vs-derived projection as Delta migration lost-data demo (P7); (5) alerts-matching tiered rule table as priority-policy rule-lens example. Distribution: bogart CI checks out catherine at a pinned rev and builds catherine-cli (cargo, cached target) — no crates.io. Deliverables: models in bogart repo, catherine check wired in bogart CI (exit codes per finding class), pilot report recording which findings were real vs noise on the live corpus. Language-neutrality demo: Clojure repo, Rust kernel, JSON interface.
notes: Dependency note (issue-review 2026-11-11): models (1)-(3) close THIS ticket at the P3+P4 gate; models (4)/(5) are follow-on adjuncts gated on P7/P8 and do not block closure — file them as separate adjunct beads when their gates pass (pattern: catherine-ga7). title: P8: rule lens — rules as subobjects with resolution policy (HYPOTHESIZED)
description: Phase 8 of docs/DESIGN.md §4.4. Rule presentation over the input domain X: rules as decidable predicates (subobjects R_i), policy = order-enrichment (PriorityOrder/FirstMatch/DeclaredDisjoint), effective region E_i = R_i \ u_{j<i} R_j. Findings: gap (uR_i != X), overlap (intersection without policy), shadow (E_i empty), derivable (R_k = R_i AND R_j). Equivalence-checkable simplification via distinguish (same total action on X, witness inputs otherwise). Rule discovery: examples + predicate vocabulary, partition-equivalence check. Attribute columns + decidable expression language (int/bool/string comparisons, AND/OR/NOT, mod) enter the kernel here. Epistemic status HYPOTHESIZED: precedent above the floor (Rust exhaustiveness, DMN hit policies) but no ct-catlab-class evidence. RED: no rule presentation type; findings not expressible. GREEN: gap/overlap/shadow/derivable findings on an enumerable domain are exact via P4 bounded search; distinguish proves or refutes rule-table equivalence with witnesses. REFACTOR: predicate expression language scoped to decidability; presentation JSON in model document. Validation (pre-registered): one kata ABOVE the triviality floor (10-20 compound rules + priority policy, pricing/eligibility table) + one second negative control NEAR the floor; killed if no unique detections above the floor. GATED on P6 (catherine-9vv) recording the schema-lens negative control first.
notes: beads also orders P8 after P7 deliberately: migration is the lower-risk post-survival phase and lands first so the rule lens builds on a stable kernel (DEP-002 rationale).

metadata.anti_goals: no new finding variants; no implicit precedence policy; killed verdict ends the scope
